articles.title: America Just Named Indian Food Its Cuisine of the Year — and It Goes Way Beyond Butter Chicken
articles.excerpt: The af&co. + Carbonate 2026 Hospitality Trends Report crowns 'Next-Gen Indian' as the defining food movement, driven by regional cooking, Gen Z spice-seekers, and a doubling of the Indian-American population.
articles.image_caption: A vibrant Indian curry blending South and North Indian preparation styles
articles.nri_angle: After decades of being reduced to butter chicken and lunch buffets, Indian cuisine's full regional diversity is finally being celebrated — a cultural validation for the diaspora that built it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Ahmedabad's Gullies to New Jersey Kitchens: The Gujarati Women Feeding the NRI Dream, One Thepla at a Time
articles.excerpt: Small home-kitchen businesses run by Gujarati women are vacuum-sealing authentic snacks for diaspora travellers, turning nostalgia into a booming cottage industry.
articles.image_caption: A traditional Gujarati thali showcasing the diverse flavours of Gujarat's home cooking
articles.nri_angle: Gujarati women's home kitchens have become the unsung supply chain behind every NRI's suitcase, turning nostalgia into a micro-economy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trial by Reel: Inside India's Bitter War Between Food Influencers and the Country's Safety Watchdog
articles.excerpt: From fake paneer accusations at celebrity restaurants to FIRs against social media creators, the battle over who polices India's food has gone viral — and the stakes are higher than likes.
articles.image_caption: Fresh paneer — the humble Indian cheese at the centre of a raging food safety debate
articles.nri_angle: Every viral 'fake food' WhatsApp forward reaches NRI kitchens worldwide, amplifying food safety anxieties for a diaspora that cares deeply about what India eats.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Chicago's Michelin List to Hudson Yards: Indienne Brings Progressive Indian Fine Dining to New York
articles.excerpt: Chef Sujan Sarkar's tasting-menu restaurant, which earned a Michelin star within its first year in Chicago, has opened a 34-seat outpost in Manhattan with $195 nine-course menus that reimagine chaat and regional Indian flavors.
articles.image_caption: Indienne opens at Hudson Yards in New York City, bringing Chef Sujan Sarkar's Michelin-starred progressive Indian cuisine (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian fine dining is now competing at the highest tier in America's most prestigious food city, signaling a dramatic shift in how the diaspora's cuisine is perceived and priced.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Two-Year-Old Indian Restaurant in Small-Town Michigan Is Competing for a World Culinary Award
articles.excerpt: KT's Rasoi in St. Joseph has been nominated for North America's Best Indian Cuisine Restaurant at the 7th annual World Culinary Awards, going up against established names across the continent.
articles.image_caption: Hyderabadi chicken dum biryani, one of KT's Rasoi's signature dishes
articles.nri_angle: A small-town Indian restaurant earning global recognition shows how diaspora food entrepreneurs are bringing authentic Indian flavors to unlikely corners of America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vada Pav, Misal Pav and a Full Bar: An Indian Family Is Betting Columbus Wants the Real Mumbai Experience
articles.excerpt: Bombay House Restaurant & Bar opens this month in the former Winking Lizard space near Polaris, bringing pan-Indian flavors and handcrafted Indian-inspired cocktails to central Ohio.
articles.image_caption: Vada pav, Mumbai's iconic street food staple, served with green and tamarind chutneys
articles.nri_angle: The Kondhare family's decision to open a pan-Indian restaurant in Columbus reflects the growing Indian-American population in Midwest cities and their hunger for food that tastes like home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: World Biryani Day Revealed India's Best-Kept Secret: The Regional Rice Revolution Coming to a City Near You
articles.excerpt: From Naga smoked pork biryani to Awadhi dum, India's regional food traditions are finally breaking free of the butter-chicken box — and diaspora kitchens are leading the charge.
articles.image_caption: A steaming plate of Hyderabadi dum biryani layered with saffron-infused rice and tender meat
articles.nri_angle: NRIs are rediscovering India's regional culinary diversity beyond the butter-chicken standard, with diaspora kitchens and restaurants leading the charge.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dosas, Biryani, and Bhangra: Toronto's Massive South Asian Street Festival Returns This Weekend
articles.excerpt: The 24th TD Festival of South Asia transforms Toronto's Little India into a two-day celebration of food, music, and diaspora community — and it is free.
articles.image_caption: A crispy masala dosa — Toronto's annual Taste of South Asia street food festival features cuisine from across the subcontinent (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The 24th TD Festival of South Asia is one of the largest diaspora cultural events in North America, showcasing how South Asian food and culture thrive in Toronto's Little India community.

articles.title: From Homeless in Manhattan to Cooking for Its Mayor: Vikas Khanna's Extraordinary Full Circle
articles.excerpt: The Michelin-starred chef who once slept on New York's streets hosted Mayor Zohran Mamdani for Iftar at his restaurant Bungalow — a reunion 25 years in the making.
articles.image_caption: Chef Vikas Khanna, the Michelin-starred Indian chef and cultural ambassador based in New York
articles.nri_angle: Vikas Khanna's journey from homeless immigrant to Michelin-starred chef hosting NYC's mayor is the quintessential diaspora success story.
